title: POC scoping - Lighthouse Health - commercial guardrails
summary: Initial POC scoping to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan and commercial guardrails for a 6-week pilot. Discussed credits, pilot terms, data residency, SOC2/SAML requirements, and path to procurement/contracting. Agreed to run latency and throughput benchmarks on ~3 representative workloads and provide a credit proposal + draft MSA.
next_steps: Jamie to send pilot credit proposal and high-level pricing (by 2026-02-02)
Sasha to share benchmark plan and test harness repo link
Customer to provide representative dataset samples and success metric spreadsheet (by 2026-01-30)
Schedule 1-hour benchmark kickoff with Lighthouse infra team (w/c 2026-02-02)
Redwood to share SOC2 summary and SSO/SAML integration notes
action_items: Jamie Patel - Send pilot pricing and credit proposal (due 2026-02-02)
Sasha Kim - Share benchmark plan, load scripts, and test harness link (due 2026-01-30)
Aisha Thompson - Upload 3 representative datasets + labeling guidelines (due 2026-01-30)
Ben Cole - Confirm procurement timeline and required contracting terms (due 2026-02-05)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-28 15:30 PST | Duration: ~42 min | Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Sasha (Redwood SE), Dr Mark (CTO), Aisha (Head ML), Ben (Procurement)

[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jamie from Redwood Inference, this is Sasha our solutions engineer. quick intro, uh, and then run through scope for the POC.
[00:12] Dr Mark: Thanks, Jamie. we want to validate that Redwood can meet latency and cost targets for our clinical summarization workload and verify the private deployment options for PHI.
[00:20] Jamie: Great. high level, we usually run a 4-6 week pilot with credits, we can customize the guardrails. today's goal is to lock success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and the procurement path.
[00:35] Aisha: For success criteria, primary is 95th pctl latency under 750ms for short notes (~512 tokens), throughput target is about 8 qps sustained, and cost per 1k tokens needs to be under our internal threshold, we'll share numbers. Also quality — rouge/clinical accuracy on our test set.
[00:55] Sasha: Okay, so latency ~750ms at 95th and 8 qps sustained. Just to check, are you open to quantized model variants for cost savings, or do you need float32 fidelity?
[01:08] Aisha: We can tolerate FP16 or int8 if quality tests pass, but must be validated against our eval prompts.
[01:14] Dr Mark: On data, PHI rules require VPC or private deployment; we prefer Redwood Private (VPC) but we'll evaluate a dedicated tenant first. Required: KMS integration and audit logs.
[01:26] Jamie: That aligns with typical enterprise flow; we can run the POC on Dedicated capacity in our region, and demonstrate Private deployment during contract discussions. We'll include notes on KMS/HSM and the audit log retention.
[01:40] Ben: Procurement question — pilot credits, are they just credits against hosted usage or is there a separate commercial pilot agreement? We need to understand path to an MSA or purchase order.
[01:50] Jamie: Good question. Our standard is to provide pilot credits that apply to usage during the pilot period plus a short pilot addendum. For larger pilots we do a pilot statement of work. Path to procurement is typically: successful POC -> commercial term sheet -> MSA / SOW -> purchase order. We'll send a sample pilot addendum and MSA redlines.
[02:08] Ben: And timing? we have fiscal quarter close at end of March so we need procurement engaged by mid-February ideally.
[02:16] Jamie: Noted. so we'll aim to have pricing and pilot credit proposal by next week, and start benchmarks early Feb.
[02:25] Sasha: On benchmarks: propose three workloads — 1) short clinical note summarization (~512 tokens input, < 128 tokens output), 2) long discharge summaries (~2k tokens), and 3) batch embeddings / search latency for our retrieval pipeline. We'll produce load scripts and an expected SLA matrix.
[02:45] Aisha: Sounds right. For throughput, the long sequence workload is the most taxing on memory; we'd like you to run with our actual seq lengths. we'll provide sample documents.
[02:56] Sasha: We'll also test with automatic batching and prefix KV cache to reduce per-token cost. note: transcript shows Redwood sometimes transcribed product names as 'Redwood Dedicated' or 'Private'.
[03:10] Dr Mark: Security checklist — SOC 2, ISO, SSO via SAML, RBAC, encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration. do you have attestation and can you share docs?
[03:22] Jamie: Yes — we'll share a SOC2 summary and the security whitepaper. SAML SSO is supported and we can show how provisioning works. For data residency we'll document region options.
[03:32] Ben: Contract terms — do you require long-term commitment for Dedicated? what about early termination for pilot?
[03:40] Jamie: Dedicated is usually reserved on a monthly commit for production, but for pilots we do short-term reserved pools or burst capacity. Pilot addendum will include termination-friendly terms; long-term reserved pricing is optional post-pilot.
[03:52] Aisha: Metrics and evaluation — we'll provide an eval harness: precision/recall on clinical entities, hallucination rate, and a human review sample. We want automated alerts if quality regresses in A/B test.
[04:10] Sasha: We can integrate Redwood Optimize to suggest batching/quantization profiles and will set up monitoring dashboards. For A/B you can pin model versions and run traffic splits.
[04:25] Jamie: On commercial guardrails — typical pilot structure we propose: 4-6 week pilot, $X in usage credits (we'll propose exact number), up to N dedicated GPU hours, and a success criteria checklist that gates next steps. If you pass, we'll provide a term sheet with committed capacity options.
[04:44] Ben: What counts as 'pass'? we need clarity — e.g., 95th pctl latency under 750ms for workload 1, error rate < 2%, and cost per 1k tokens below threshold.
[04:55] Jamie: Exactly. we'll draft a success criteria table and include quantitative thresholds. We'll also include acceptance testing steps.
[05:05] Dr Mark: Benchmarks — who runs them? your team or ours? we need repeatability and reproducibility.
[05:13] Sasha: Our SEs run the initial baseline in our environment with your dataset, then we provide the scripts so you can reproduce locally or in your infra. We'll deliver the scripts, logs, and a results spreadsheet.
[05:26] Aisha: For cost modeling, can you provide per-token and per-hour GPU cost breakdowns and an estimate for our observed traffic distribution?
[05:34] Jamie: Yes — we'll provide a token-level cost breakdown and run a sample cost projection based on the workload mix you send. We'll include options for quantized model variants and batching impacts.
[05:44] Ben: Procurement note — we'll likely need a pilot statement of work and a simple PO. MSA negotiation can be parallel but we need basic liability and data terms to sign the SOW.
[05:56] Jamie: Understood. we'll provide a draft pilot SOW and sample MSA redlines.
[06:04] Sasha: Quick technical note on private deployments — if you go VPC Private, network setup usually requires a small infra window; we can help with a runbook. KV cache and prefix caching work the same in Dedicated and Private. There might be some kernel-level perf differences on-prem, we'll note them.
[06:20] Aisha: Good to know. we may try Dedicated first to validate perf and cost, then evaluate the Private deployment for PHI.
[06:28] Dr Mark: Timeline check — we want benchmarks completed by Feb 14 so procurement can review by Feb 21. Is that feasible?
[06:34] Jamie: Yes, if we get datasets by Jan 30 and sign pilot addendum by Feb 2 we can target benchmarks the week of Feb 9-14.
[06:43] Sasha: We'll need access to sample data and any network IP allowlists if you want us to run in your VPC; otherwise we can run in our Dedicated env with masked data.
[06:53] Aisha: We'll provide masked samples first. and access details if needed.
[07:00] Ben: On credits — do credits expire? can they be applied to post-pilot committed spend?
[07:06] Jamie: Pilot credits typically expire at the end of the pilot period but are sometimes applied as discounts on first invoice if you convert to committed spend. We'll put options in the proposal.
[07:16] Dr Mark: Any hidden costs like data egress or long-term storage?
[07:20] Jamie: We'll call out egress and storage in the pricing sheet; most pilot usage is compute-heavy.
[07:27] Aisha: For benchmarks, please include both P95 and p99 latencies and tail behavior. We care about 95th but will look at 99th for SLA decisions.
[07:36] Sasha: Noted. We'll include p50/p95/p99, throughput, GPU utilization, and tokens/sec.
[07:44] Jamie: Next steps recap — Jamie sends credit proposal and pricing; Sasha shares benchmark plan; Lighthouse shares datasets; schedule kickoff.
[07:55] Ben: Sounds good. any other vendor questions? we mentioned Anthropic earlier — just evaluating strengths.
[08:02] Jamie: no problem. we'll include a competitive note in the proposal.
[08:08] Dr Mark: Great. thanks all.

[End of recording]

Notes: Transcript has occasional imperfect transcription (product names, acronyms). SE action item to share test harness repo. Pilot guardrails: 4-6 weeks, credits applied during pilot, pilot addendum + optional SOW, path to MSA/PO.
